facts.fact: The article reports that reading its sample paragraph aloud takes about 20 seconds, which the author uses to illustrate how little time a 30-second TV spot leaves.
facts.quote: Read this paragraph out loud, and you've already used about 20 seconds.

facts.fact: The article advises small businesses to plan for at least 4-6 weeks before evaluating TV campaign success.
facts.quote: Plan for at least 4-6 weeks before evaluating success

facts.fact: The article states viewers need to see a TV ad about 3-5 times at minimum before it sticks.
facts.quote: You need viewers to see your ad multiple times (3-5 exposures minimum) before it sticks.

facts.fact: The article suggests starting with at least $50-100 for a focused TV advertising test.
facts.quote: Start with at least [$50-100 for a focused test](https://adwave.com/pricing/)

facts.fact: The article gives an example of a $100-per-month budget run for six months as too thin to build memory, and contrasts it with running $300 for two weeks.
facts.quote: $100 per month for six months sounds reasonable, but it means so few impressions each month that no one sees your ad enough times to remember it.

facts.fact: The article advises stopping a TV campaign only after 6 or more weeks with zero measurable impact.
facts.quote: After 6+ weeks with zero measurable impact

facts.fact: The article states that Google Trends is free to use for tracking brand search volume.
facts.quote: Brand search volume (Google Trends is free)

facts.fact: The article says the first 3 seconds of a TV ad determine whether viewers pay attention or zone out.
facts.quote: The first 3 seconds determine whether viewers pay attention or zone out.

facts.fact: The article was published on November 7, 2025.
Adwave advises planning for at least four weeks of consistent TV advertising before drawing conclusions about results.
facts.quote: Plan for at least four weeks of consistent advertising before drawing conclusions.

facts.fact: Adwave advises measuring TV campaign results over several months rather than a single short campaign.
Adwave offers a free option to create a first TV ad through its try-free sign-up.
